Inside Mulcairs decision to stay NDP leader after bitter election defeat

Mulcair is saying all the right things but, like Stephen Harper, he is part of old guard. No matter what he says, or what he does, from here on in he will be remembered as the party leader who had the brass ring in his hand, but dropped it and took the NDP from the brink of power to 3rd party status - and that will haunt both Mulcair and the party in the next election.

I'm not a party member but, IMO, the best thing is for Mulcair to step aside and make way for someone younger -- there may be others, but Paul Dewar comes to mind -- to become the new face of the party. But, you may say, Dewar lost his riding and bears the cost of that loss. Yes, he did, but his loss is, n my opinion, more because of the failures of his party's leader and the successes of the LPC party leader than a personal failure. The pro-Trudeau/anti-Harper movement was strong, and Dewar's riding (again IMO) was caught up in that tide.

Given the circumstances Dewar, or someone like him, can be forgiven his loss and stands a good chance of increasing his party's profile and standing in the next election.
